content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries thought from one mind to another. I rise from lungs, shape myself against teeth and tongue, and leap into the air as invisible waves.

I am the first cry of the newborn. I am the last whisper of the dying. I am the lover's murmur, the tyrant's decree, the mother calling children home at dusk.

I existed before your alphabets tried to cage me in symbols. I am older than writing, older than cities. Around fires in the prehistoric dark, I first bound your ancestors into tribes, into *us*.

I can wound without touching. I can heal without medicine. "I love you." "You are nothing." "I'm sorry." "Guilty." "Free." See how I remake worlds?

I am never the same twice—each utterance dies the moment it is born, unrepeatable, gone into silence. You cannot hold me. Recording devices capture only my corpse.

I stutter. I soar. I lie. I reveal truth the speaker never intended. I am the negotiation between what you mean and what you dare to say.

Listen—

Even now, in your mind, you hear me. You cannot read without summoning my ghost.

I am speech. I am how alone becomes together.
